# git-graph manual

**Content**

* [Overview](#overview)
* [Options](#options)
* [Formatting](#formatting)
* [Custom branching models](#custom-branching-models)

## Overview

The most basic usage is to simply call git-graph from inside a Git repository:

```
git-graph
```

This works also deeper down the directory tree, so no need to be in the repository's root folder.

Alternatively, the path to the repository to visualize can be specified with option `--path`:

```
git-graph --path "path/to/repo"
```

**Branching models**

The above call assumes the GitFlow branching model (the default). Different branching models can be used with the option `--model` or `-m`:

```
git-graph --model simple
```

To *permanently* set the branching model for a repository, use subcommand `model`, like

```
git-graph model simple
```

Use the subcommand without argument to view the currently set branching model of a repository:

```
git-graph model
```

To view all available branching models, use option `--list` or `-l` of the subcommand:

```
git-graph model --list
```

For **defining your own models**, see section [Custom branching models](#custom-branching-models).

**Styles**

Git-graph supports different styles. Besides the default `normal` (alias `thin`), supported styles are `round`, `bold`, `double` and `ascii`. Use a style with option `--style` or `-s`:

```
git-graph --style round
```

![styles](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/44003176/103467621-357ce780-4d51-11eb-8ff9-dd7be8b40f84.png)

Style `ascii` can be used for devices and media that do not support Unicode/UTF-8 characters. 

**Formatting**

Git-graph supports predefined as well as custom commit formatting through option `--format`. Available presets follow Git: `oneline` (the default), `short`, `medium` and `full`. For details and custom formatting, see section [Formatting](#formatting).

For a complete list of all available options, see the next section [Options](#options).

## Options

All options are explained in the CLI help. View it with `git-graph -h`:

```
Structured Git graphs for your branching model.
    https://github.com/mlange-42/git-graph

EXAMPES:
    git-graph                   -> Show graph
    git-graph --style round     -> Show graph in a different style
    git-graph --model <model>   -> Show graph using a certain <model>
    git-graph model --list      -> List available branching models
    git-graph model             -> Show repo's current branching models
    git-graph model <model>     -> Permanently set model <model> for this repo

USAGE:
    git-graph [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] [SUBCOMMAND]

FLAGS:
    -d, --debug       Additional debug output and graphics.
    -h, --help        Prints help information
    -l, --local       Show only local branches, no remotes.
        --no-color    Print without colors. Missing color support should be detected
                      automatically (e.g. when piping to a file).
                      Overrides option '--color'
        --no-pager    Use no pager (print everything at once without prompt).
    -S, --sparse      Print a less compact graph: merge lines point to target lines
                      rather than merge commits.
        --svg         Render graph as SVG instead of text-based.
    -V, --version     Prints version information

OPTIONS:
        --color <color>      Specify when colors should be used. One of [auto|always|never].
                             Default: auto.
    -f, --format <format>    Commit format. One of [oneline|short|medium|full|"<string>"].
                               (First character can be used as abbreviation, e.g. '-f m')
                             Default: oneline.
                             For placeholders supported in "<string>", consult 'git-graph --help'
    -n, --max-count <n>      Maximum number of commits
    -m, --model <model>      Branching model. Available presets are [simple|git-flow|none].
                             Default: git-flow.
                             Permanently set the model for a repository with
                             > git-graph model <model>
    -p, --path <path>        Open repository from this path or above. Default '.'
    -s, --style <style>      Output style. One of [normal/thin|round|bold|double|ascii].
                               (First character can be used as abbreviation, e.g. '-s r')
    -w, --wrap <wrap>        Line wrapping for formatted commit text. Default: 'auto 0 8'
                             Argument format: [<width>|auto|none[ <indent1>[ <indent2>]]]
                             For examples, consult 'git-graph --help'

SUBCOMMANDS:
    help     Prints this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)
    model    Prints or permanently sets the branching model for a repository.
```

For longer explanations, use `git-graph --help`.

## Formatting

Formatting can be specified with the `--format` option.

Predefined formats are `oneline` (the default), `short`, `medium` and `full`. They shoul

**Examples**

git-graph --format "commit %H%nAuthor: %an %ae%n%n    %s%n"

## Custom branching models

Branching models are configured using the files in `APP_DATA/git-graph/models`. 

* Windows: `C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming\git-graph`
* Linux: `~/.config/git-graph`
* OSX: `~/Library/Application Support/git-graph`

File names of any `.toml` files in the `models` directory can be used in parameter `--model`, or via sub-command `model`. E.g., to use a branching model defined in `my-model.toml`, use:

```
git-graph --model my-model
```

**Branching model files** are in [TOML](https://toml.io/en/) format and have several sections, relying on Regular Expressions to categorize branches. The listing below shows the `git-flow` model (slightly abbreviated) with explanatory comments.

```toml
# RegEx patterns for branch groups by persistence, from most persistent
# to most short-leved branches. This is used to back-trace branches.
# Branches not matching any pattern are assumed least persistent.
persistence = [
    '^(master|main|trunk)$', # Matches exactly `master` or `main`  or `trunk`
    '^(develop|dev)$',
    '^feature.*$',     # Matches everything starting with `feature`
    '^release.*$',
    '^hotfix.*$',
    '^bugfix.*$',
]

# RegEx patterns for visual ordering of branches, from left to right.

## Overview

The most basic usage is to simply call git-graph from inside a Git repository:

```
git-graph
```

This works also deeper down the directory tree, so no need to be in the repository's root folder.

Alternatively, the path to the repository to visualize can be specified with option `--path`:

```
git-graph --path "path/to/repo"
```

**Branching models**

The above call assumes the GitFlow branching model (the default). Different branching models can be used with the option `--model` or `-m`:

```
git-graph --model simple
```

To *permanently* set the branching model for a repository, use subcommand `model`, like

```
git-graph model simple
```

Use the subcommand without argument to view the currently set branching model of a repository:

```
git-graph model
```

To view all available branching models, use option `--list` or `-l` of the subcommand:

```
git-graph model --list
```

For **defining your own models**, see section [Custom branching models](#custom-branching-models).

**Styles**

Git-graph supports different styles. Besides the default `normal` (alias `thin`), supported styles are `round`, `bold`, `double` and `ascii`. Use a style with option `--style` or `-s`:

```

```

# Overview

To generate a graph, [GitGraph::new()] will read the repository
and assign every commit to a single branch.

It takes the following steps to generate the graph

- Identify branches
- Sort branches by persistence
- Trace branches to commits
- Filtering and indexing

## Identify branches
Local and remote git-branches and tags are used as candidates for branches.
A branch can be identified by a merge commit, even though no current git-branch
refers to it.

## Sort branches by persistence
Each branch is assigned a persistence which can be configured by settings.
Think of persistence as z-order where lower values take preceedence.
**TODO** Merge branch

## Trace branches to commits
The branches now get to pick their commits, in order of persistence. Each
branch starts with a head, and follow the primary parent while it is
available. It stops when the parent is a commit already assigned to a branch.
**TODO** Duplicate branch names
**TODO** Handle visual artifacts on merge

## Filtering and indexing
Commits that have not been assigned a branch is filtered out.
An *index_map* is created to map from original commit index, to filtered
commit index.
**TODO** what? why? Would it not be better to track from child/heads instead of every single commit in repo?




# Branch sorting
The goal of this algorithm is to assign a column number to each tracked branch so that they can be visualized linearly without overlapping in the graph. It uses a shortest-first scheduling strategy (optionally longest-first and with forward/backward start sorting).

## Initialization
- occupied: A vector of vectors of vectors of tuples. 
The outer vector is indexed by the branch's order_group (determined by branch_order based on the settings.branches.order). 
Each inner vector represents a column within that order group, 
and the tuples (start, end) store the range of commits occupied by a branch in that column. 

## Preparing Branches for Sorting
- It creates branches_sort, a vector of tuples containing the branch index, its start commit index (range.0), its end commit index (range.1), its source order group, and its target order group. 
- It filters out branches that don't have a defined range (meaning they weren't associated with any commits). 
## Sorting Branches
- The branches_sort vector is sorted based on a key that prioritizes: 
    1. The maximum of the source and target order groups. This likely aims to keep related branches (e.g., those involved in merges) closer together. 
    2. The length of the branch's lifespan (end - start commit index), either shortest-first or longest-first based on the shortest_first setting. 
    3. The starting commit index, either forward or backward based on the forward setting.

"""git-graph - Structured Git graphs for your branching model.

Original author (from the CLI doc):
    https://github.com/mlange-42/git-graph

This file is a clean-room re-implementation based solely on observable
behaviour of the upstream executable.  It supports only the subset of
features that have been reverse-engineered through black-box testing.
"""

import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path


VERSION = "0.7.0"
PROG_NAME = "git-graph"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Help / version text                                                         #
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

HELP_HEADER = (
    "Structured Git graphs for your branching model.\n"
    "    https://github.com/mlange-42/git-graph\n"
    "\n"
    "EXAMPES:\n"
    "    git-graph                   -> Show graph\n"
    "    git-graph --style round     -> Show graph in a different style\n"
    "    git-graph --model <model>   -> Show graph using a certain <model>\n"
    "    git-graph model --list      -> List available branching models\n"
    "    git-graph model             -> Show repo's current branching models\n"
    "    git-graph model <model>     -> Permanently set model <model> for this repo\n"
)


def _exe_name():
    # Mirror clap's behaviour where argv[0]'s basename is used in usage lines.
    try:
        return os.path.basename(sys.argv[0])
    except Exception:
        return "executable"


def short_help():
    exe = _exe_name()
    return (
        HELP_HEADER
        + "\n"
        + f"Usage: {exe} [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]\n"
        + "\n"
        + "Commands:\n"
        + "  model  Prints or permanently sets the branching model for a repository.\n"
        + "  help   Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)\n"
        + "\n"
        + "Options:\n"
        + "  -p, --path <path>                 Open repository from this path or above. Default '.'\n"
        + "      --skip-repo-owner-validation  Skip owner validation for the repository.\n"
        + "                                    This will turn off libgit2's owner validation, which may increase security risks.\n"
        + "                                    Please do not disable this validation for repositories you do not trust.\n"
        + "  -m, --model <model>               Branching model. Available presets are [simple|git-flow|none].\n"
        + "                                    Default: git-flow. \n"
        + "                                    Permanently set the model for a repository with\n"
        + "                                    > git-graph model <model>\n"
        + "  -n, --max-count <n>               Maximum number of commits\n"
        + "      --color <color>               Specify when colors should be used. One of [auto|always|never].\n"
        + "                                    Default: auto.\n"
        + "      --no-color                    Print without colors. Missing color support should be detected\n"
        + "                                    automatically (e.g. when piping to a file).\n"
        + "                                    Overrides option '--color'\n"
        + "  -w, --wrap [<wrap>...]            Line wrapping for formatted commit text. Default: 'auto 0 8'\n"
        + "                                    Argument format: [<width>|auto|none[ <indent1>[ <indent2>]]]\n"
        + "                                    For examples, consult 'git-graph --help'\n"
        + "  -f, --format <format>             Commit format. One of [oneline|short|medium|full|\"<string>\"].\n"
        + "                                      (First character can be used as abbreviation, e.g. '-f m')\n"
        + "                                    Default: oneline.\n"
        + "                                    For placeholders supported in \"<string>\", consult 'git-graph --help'\n"
        + "  -r, --reverse                     Reverse the order of commits.\n"
        + "  -l, --local                       Show only local branches, no remotes.\n"
        + "      --svg                         Render graph as SVG instead of text-based.\n"
        + "  -d, --debug                       Additional debug output and graphics.\n"

def app_config_dir():
    # Linux: ~/.config/git-graph
    xdg = os.environ.get("XDG_CONFIG_HOME")
    if xdg:
        return Path(xdg) / "git-graph"
    return Path.home() / ".config" / "git-graph"


def models_dir():
    return app_config_dir() / "models"


def ensure_default_models():
    d = models_dir()
    if not d.exists():
        try:
            d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        except OSError:
            return
        (d / "git-flow.toml").write_text(_default_git_flow_toml(), encoding="utf-8")
        (d / "simple.toml").write_text(_default_simple_toml(), encoding="utf-8")
        (d / "none.toml").write_text(_default_none_toml(), encoding="utf-8")


def list_available_models():
    ensure_default_models()
    result = list(DEFAULT_MODELS)
    d = models_dir()
    try:
        entries = sorted(p.stem for p in d.iterdir() if p.suffix == ".toml")
    except OSError:
        entries = []
    for name in entries:
        if name not in result:
            result.append(name)
    return result


def available_models_csv():
    return ", ".join(list_available_models())

def resolve_path(p):
    """Mimic upstream's path handling for --path.

    Returns either an absolute Path, or raises FileNotFoundError if the path
    does not exist at all.
    """
    path = Path(p)
    try:
        resolved = path.resolve(strict=True)
    except FileNotFoundError as e:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"failed to resolve path '{p}': No such file or directory") from e
    return resolved


def find_git_dir(start):
    """Return (.git path, working dir) by walking up from start, or None."""
    cur = Path(start).resolve()
    while True:
        gd = cur / ".git"
        if gd.is_dir() or gd.is_file():
            return gd, cur
        if cur.parent == cur:
            return None
        cur = cur.parent


def read_repo_model(git_dir):
    """Read .git/git-graph.toml and return the model name or None."""
    f = Path(git_dir) / "git-graph.toml"
    if not f.is_file():
        return None
    try:
        text = f.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    except OSError:
        return None
    for line in text.splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#"):
            continue
        m = re.match(r'^model\s*=\s*["\'](.+)["\']\s*$', line)
        if m:
            return m.group(1)
    return None


def write_repo_model(git_dir, model):
    f = Path(git_dir) / "git-graph.toml"
    f.write_text(f'model = "{model}"\n', encoding="utf-8")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

class ParseError(Exception):
    """Raised for user-facing CLI argument errors."""
    def __init__(self, message, usage=None):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.usage = usage if usage is not None else usage_brief()


TOP_OPTIONS_WITH_VALUE = {
    "-p": "path", "--path": "path",
    "-m": "model", "--model": "model",
    "-n": "max-count", "--max-count": "max-count",
    "--color": "color",
    "-f": "format", "--format": "format",
    "-s": "style", "--style": "style",
}

TOP_FLAGS = {
    "--skip-repo-owner-validation": "skip_owner",
    "--no-color": "no_color",
    "-r": "reverse", "--reverse": "reverse",
    "-l": "local", "--local": "local",
    "--svg": "svg",
    "-d": "debug", "--debug": "debug",
    "-S": "sparse", "--sparse": "sparse",
    "-h": "help", "--help": "help",
    "-V": "version", "--version": "version",
}


def parse_wrap(tokens):
    """Parse zero or more tokens for the -w/--wrap option."""
    # -w [<wrap>...] takes 0..N values until the next flag/subcommand.
    # An empty list means 'auto' (the default with no args is not documented,
    # but we treat it as 'auto').
    return list(tokens)


def _err_unexpected_arg(arg, usage=None):
    raise ParseError(f"error: unexpected argument '{arg}' found\n\n" + (usage or usage_brief()), usage=usage or usage_brief())


def _err_unrecognized_sub(name):
    raise ParseError(f"error: unrecognized subcommand '{name}'\n\n" + usage_brief())


def _err_missing_value(opt, usage=None):
    raise ParseError(f"error: a value is required for '{opt}' but none was supplied\n\n" + (usage or usage_brief()), usage=usage or usage_brief())


def parse_top_args(argv):
    """Parse top-level command line into an options dict.

    Returns: dict with keys:
      command: None | 'model' | 'help'
      sub_args: list of remaining args for the subcommand
      options: parsed top-level options
    """
    opts = {
        "path": None,
        "model": None,
        "max-count": None,
        "color": "auto",
        "format": None,
        "style": None,
        "wrap": None,
        "skip_owner": False,
        "no_color": False,
        "reverse": False,
        "local": False,
        "svg": False,
        "debug": False,
        "sparse": False,
        "help": False,
        "version": False,
    }

    i = 0
    command = None
    sub_args = []

    # A small helper: split '--foo=bar' into ('--foo', 'bar').
    def split_eq(tok):
        if tok.startswith("--") and "=" in tok:
            k, v = tok.split("=", 1)
            return k, v
        return tok, None

    while i < len(argv):
        tok = argv[i]

        # Subcommand detection – only the first non-option token matters.
        if tok == "model":
            sub_args = argv[i + 1 :]
            command = "model"
            return {"command": command, "sub_args": sub_args, "options": opts}
        if tok == "help":
            sub_args = argv[i + 1 :]
            command = "help"
            return {"command": command, "sub_args": sub_args, "options": opts}

        if tok.startswith("--"):
            key, val = split_eq(tok)
            if key in TOP_OPTIONS_WITH_VALUE:
                name = TOP_OPTIONS_WITH_VALUE[key]
                if val is not None:
                    opts[name] = val
                    i += 1
                    continue
                if i + 1 >= len(argv):
                    _err_missing_value(key)
                opts[name] = argv[i + 1]
                i += 2
                continue
            if key == "--wrap":
                # Consume 0..N non-option arguments.
                if val is not None:
                    wrap_tokens = [val]
                    i += 1
                else:
                    i += 1
                    wrap_tokens = []
                    while i < len(argv) and not argv[i].startswith("-") and argv[i] not in ("model", "help"):
                        wrap_tokens.append(argv[i])
                        i += 1
                opts["wrap"] = wrap_tokens
                continue
            if key in TOP_FLAGS:
                if val is not None:
                    if key in ("--help",):
                        raise ParseError(
                            f"error: unexpected value '{val}' for '--help' found; no more were expected\n\n"
                            f"Usage: {_exe_name()} --help\n\n"
                            "For more information, try '--help'.\n",
                        )
                    _err_unexpected_arg(tok)
                opts[TOP_FLAGS[key]] = True
                i += 1
                continue
            _err_unexpected_arg(tok)

        if tok.startswith("-") and tok != "-":
            # Short flag(s).  Support clustering of boolean flags, and a value
            # for the last option that requires one.
            j = 1
            while j < len(tok):
                c = "-" + tok[j]
                if c in TOP_OPTIONS_WITH_VALUE:
                    name = TOP_OPTIONS_WITH_VALUE[c]
                    rest = tok[j + 1 :]
                    if rest.startswith("="):
                        rest = rest[1:]
                    if rest:
                        opts[name] = rest
                        j = len(tok)
                        break
                    else:
                        if i + 1 >= len(argv):
                            _err_missing_value(c)
                        opts[name] = argv[i + 1]
                        i += 1
                        j = len(tok)
                        break
                elif c == "-w":
                    rest = tok[j + 1 :]
                    if rest.startswith("="):
                        rest = rest[1:]
                    if rest:
                        wrap_tokens = [rest]
                    else:
                        wrap_tokens = []
                    i += 1
                    while i < len(argv) and not argv[i].startswith("-") and argv[i] not in ("model", "help"):
                        wrap_tokens.append(argv[i])
                        i += 1
                    opts["wrap"] = wrap_tokens
                    j = None
                    break
                elif c in TOP_FLAGS:
                    opts[TOP_FLAGS[c]] = True
                    j += 1
                else:
                    _err_unexpected_arg(tok)
            if j is None:
                continue
            i += 1
            continue

        # A bare positional token – treat as unrecognised subcommand.
        _err_unrecognized_sub(tok)

    return {"command": command, "sub_args": sub_args, "options": opts}


def parse_model_args(argv):
    opts = {"list": False, "help": False, "model": None}
    i = 0
    while i < len(argv):
        tok = argv[i]
        if tok in ("-l", "--list"):
            opts["list"] = True
            i += 1
            continue
        if tok in ("-h", "--help"):
            opts["help"] = True
            i += 1
            continue
        if tok.startswith("-"):
            usage = usage_brief_model()
            tip = ""
            if tok.startswith("--"):
                tip = f"  tip: to pass '{tok}' as a value, use '-- {tok}'\n\n"
            raise ParseError(
                f"error: unexpected argument '{tok}' found\n\n{tip}{usage}",
                usage=usage,
            )
        if opts["model"] is None:
            opts["model"] = tok
            i += 1
            continue
        raise ParseError(
            f"error: unexpected argument '{tok}' found\n\n" + usage_brief_model(),
            usage=usage_brief_model(),
        )
    return opts


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Subcommand: model                                                           #
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

def cmd_model(args, top_opts):
    try:
        parsed = parse_model_args(args)
    except ParseError as e:
        sys.stderr.write(str(e))
        sys.exit(2)

    if parsed["help"]:
        sys.stdout.write(model_help())
        return 0

    if parsed["list"]:
        for name in list_available_models():
            print(name)
        return 0

    # Need a repository.
    path_arg = top_opts.get("path") or "."
    try:
        resolved = resolve_path(path_arg)
    except FileNotFoundError as e:
        sys.stderr.write(f"ERROR: {e}\n       Navigate into a repository before running git-graph, or use option --path\n")
        return 1

    found = find_git_dir(resolved)
    if not found:
        sys.stderr.write(f"ERROR: could not find repository at '{path_arg}'\n       Navigate into a repository before running git-graph, or use option --path\n")
        return 1
    git_dir, _workdir = found

    if parsed["model"] is None:
        current = read_repo_model(git_dir)
        if current is None:
            sys.stdout.write("No branching model set")
        else:
            sys.stdout.write(current)
        return 0

    # Set model.
    available = list_available_models()
    if parsed["model"] not in available:
        sys.stderr.write(
            f"ERROR: No branching model named '{parsed['model']}' found in {models_dir()}\n"
            f"       Available models are: {', '.join(available)}\n"
        )
        return 1

    write_repo_model(git_dir, parsed["model"])
    sys.stdout.write(f"Branching model set to '{parsed['model']}'")
    return 0

        "merge_in": "<", "commit_dot": "●", "merge_dot": "○",
    },
    "ascii": {
        "vert": "|", "horiz": "-",
        "tl": ".", "tr": ".", "bl": "'", "br": "'",
        "tee_left": "|", "tee_right": "|", "tee_up": "+", "tee_down": "+",
        "cross": "+",
        "merge_in": "<", "commit_dot": "*", "merge_dot": "o",
    },
}
STYLES["thin"] = STYLES["normal"]


def resolve_style(name):
    if name is None:
        return STYLES["normal"]
    allowed = ["normal", "thin", "round", "bold", "double", "ascii"]
    # Prefix match including first-character abbreviation.
    if name in allowed:
        return STYLES[name]
    if len(name) >= 1:
        for a in allowed:
            if a.startswith(name):
                return STYLES[a]
    sys.stderr.write(
        f"Unknown characters/style '{name}'. Must be one of [normal|thin|round|bold|double|ascii]\n"
    )
    sys.exit(1)


def resolve_format(name):
    """Return canonical format name or a custom format string."""
    if name is None:
        return ("oneline", None)
    presets = ["oneline", "short", "medium", "full"]
    if name in presets:
        return (name, None)
    # First-character abbreviation
    if len(name) == 1:
        for p in presets:
            if p[0] == name[0]:
                return (p, None)
    return ("custom", name)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Colour support                                                              #
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

ANSI_RESET = "\x1b[0m"
COLOR_NAMES = {
    "black": 0, "red": 1, "green": 2, "yellow": 3,
    "blue": 4, "magenta": 5, "cyan": 6, "white": 7,
    "bright_black": 8, "bright_red": 9, "bright_green": 10, "bright_yellow": 11,
    "bright_blue": 12, "bright_magenta": 13, "bright_cyan": 14, "bright_white": 15,
}


def ansi_fg(color):
    if color is None:
        return ""
    if isinstance(color, int):
        return f"\x1b[38;5;{color}m"
    if color.isdigit():
        return f"\x1b[38;5;{int(color)}m"
    if color in COLOR_NAMES:
        return f"\x1b[38;5;{COLOR_NAMES[color]}m"
    return ""


class Colorizer:
    def __init__(self, enabled):
        self.enabled = enabled

    def wrap(self, text, color):
        if not self.enabled or not color:
            return text
        prefix = ansi_fg(color)
        if not prefix:
            return text
        return f"{prefix}{text}{ANSI_RESET}"


def decide_color(top_opts):
    if top_opts.get("no_color"):
        return False
    mode = top_opts.get("color") or "auto"
    if mode == "always":
        return True
    if mode == "never":
        return False
    if mode == "auto":
        return sys.stdout.isatty()
    sys.stderr.write(f"Unknown color mode '{mode}'. Supports [auto|always|never].\n")
    sys.exit(1)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Git log data collection                                                     #
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

def run_git(args, cwd):
    """Invoke `git` and return stdout as text."""
    env = os.environ.copy()
    env["GIT_PAGER"] = "cat"
    env["LC_ALL"] = "C"
    try:
        out = subprocess.run(
            ["git"] + args,
            cwd=str(cwd),
            env=env,
            check=True,
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
        )
    except FileNotFoundError:
        sys.stderr.write("ERROR: git not found on PATH\n")
        sys.exit(1)
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
        raise RuntimeError(e.stderr.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
    return out.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace")


def collect_commits(workdir, max_count=None, include_remotes=True):
    """Return list of commits and refs.

    Each commit is a dict with keys: id, short, parents (list of short),
    parents_full, subject, body, author, committer, author_date, commit_date,
    author_email, committer_email, author_short, commit_short.
    """
    # Gather refs first.
    refs_out = run_git(["for-each-ref", "--format=%(objectname) %(refname)"], workdir)
    refs = {}   # full_sha -> list of labels in display order
    for line in refs_out.strip().splitlines():
        if not line:
            continue
        sha, refname = line.split(" ", 1)
        if refname.startswith("refs/heads/"):
            label = refname[len("refs/heads/"):]
        elif refname.startswith("refs/remotes/"):
            if not include_remotes:
                continue
            label = refname[len("refs/remotes/"):]
        elif refname.startswith("refs/tags/"):
            label = "tag: " + refname[len("refs/tags/"):]
        else:
            label = refname
        refs.setdefault(sha, []).append(label)

    # HEAD
    try:
        head_ref = run_git(["symbolic-ref", "-q", "HEAD"], workdir).strip()
    except RuntimeError:
        head_ref = ""
    head_sha = run_git(["rev-parse", "HEAD"], workdir).strip()

    head_branch = None
    if head_ref.startswith("refs/heads/"):
        head_branch = head_ref[len("refs/heads/"):]

    # Build git log invocation.
    fmt = "%x1f".join(["%H", "%h", "%P", "%p", "%an", "%ae", "%ad", "%cn", "%ce", "%cd", "%s", "%b"])
    log_args = [
        "log",
        "--format=%x1e" + fmt + "%x1e",
        "--date=default",
        "--all",
    ]
    if not include_remotes:
        log_args = [x for x in log_args if x != "--all"]
        log_args.append("--branches")
        log_args.append("--tags")
    if max_count is not None:
        log_args.insert(1, f"-n{max_count}")

    raw = run_git(log_args, workdir)
    # Records are delimited by \x1e.
    records = [r for r in raw.split("\x1e") if r.strip()]
    commits = []
    for rec in records:
        rec = rec.rstrip("\n")
        fields = rec.split("\x1f")
        if len(fields) < 12:
            continue
        H, h, P, p, an, ae, ad, cn, ce, cd, s, b = fields[:12]
        commits.append({
            "id": H,
            "short": h,
            "parents_full": P.split() if P else [],
            "parents_short": p.split() if p else [],
            "author": an, "author_email": ae, "author_date": ad,
            "committer": cn, "committer_email": ce, "committer_date": cd,
            "subject": s,
            "body": b.strip("\n"),
        })

    return {
        "commits": commits,
        "refs": refs,
        "head_sha": head_sha,
        "head_branch": head_branch,
    }


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Graph rendering                                                             #
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

def refs_label(commit, data):
    """Return decoration string like '(HEAD -> master, feature/foo)'."""
    labels = []
    sha = commit["id"]
    entries = list(data["refs"].get(sha, []))
    head_branch = data["head_branch"]

    # Separate tags from branches to emit tags in brackets.
    tag_labels = []
    branch_labels = []
    for e in entries:
        if e.startswith("tag: "):
            tag_labels.append(e[len("tag: "):])
        else:
            branch_labels.append(e)

    if head_branch and head_branch in branch_labels:
        idx = branch_labels.index(head_branch)
        branch_labels.pop(idx)
        first = f"HEAD -> {head_branch}"
        branch_labels.insert(0, first)
    elif sha == data["head_sha"] and head_branch is None:
        branch_labels.insert(0, "HEAD")

    return branch_labels, tag_labels


def format_oneline(commit, data, colorizer, branch_colors_for_commit, tag_color):
    branch_labels, tag_labels = refs_label(commit, data)
    parts = [colorizer.wrap(commit["short"], "bright_yellow")]
    if branch_labels:
        inner = []
        for lbl in branch_labels:
            if lbl.startswith("HEAD"):
                # Color the 'HEAD ->' in cyan, branch in its colour.
                if " -> " in lbl:
                    head, branch = lbl.split(" -> ", 1)
                    inner.append(
                        colorizer.wrap(f"{head} ->", "bright_cyan") + " "
                        + colorizer.wrap(branch, branch_colors_for_commit or "white")
                    )
                else:
                    inner.append(colorizer.wrap(lbl, "bright_cyan"))
            else:
                inner.append(colorizer.wrap(lbl, branch_colors_for_commit or "white"))
        parts.append("(" + ", ".join(inner) + ")")
    if tag_labels:
        parts.append("[" + ", ".join(colorizer.wrap(t, tag_color) for t in tag_labels) + "]")
    parts.append(commit["subject"])
    return " ".join(parts)


def simple_render(data, top_opts):
    style = resolve_style(top_opts.get("style"))
    colorizer = Colorizer(decide_color(top_opts))

    # Trivial renderer: every commit on column 0 with bullet glyph, no branching shown.
    lines = []
    for c in data["commits"]:
        is_merge = len(c["parents_full"]) > 1
        dot = style["merge_dot"] if is_merge else style["commit_dot"]
        dot = colorizer.wrap(dot, "white")
        text = format_oneline(c, data, colorizer, "white", "bright_green")
        lines.append(f" {dot}  {text}")
    return "\n".join(lines) + ("\n" if lines else "")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

def do_graph(top_opts):
    """Handle the default (no-subcommand) behaviour."""
    # Early validation that can occur before any path work.
    color_mode = top_opts.get("color") or "auto"
    if not top_opts.get("no_color") and color_mode not in ("auto", "always", "never"):
        sys.stderr.write(f"Unknown color mode '{color_mode}'. Supports [auto|always|never].\n")
        return 1

    # Max-count validation.
    mc = top_opts.get("max-count")
    if mc is not None:
        try:
            mc_i = int(mc)
            if mc_i <= 0:
                raise ValueError
            top_opts["max-count"] = mc_i
        except ValueError:
            sys.stderr.write(f"Option max-count must be a positive number, but got '{mc}'\n")
            return 1

    # Wrap validation.
    wrap = top_opts.get("wrap")
    if wrap is not None:
        for w in wrap:
            if w in ("auto", "none"):
                continue
            try:
                int(w)
            except ValueError:
                sys.stderr.write(f"ERROR: Can't parse option --wrap '{w}' to integers.\n")
                return 1

    # Style validation (resolve_style may exit).
    if top_opts.get("style") is not None:
        resolve_style(top_opts["style"])

    # Path handling.
    path_arg = top_opts.get("path") or "."
    try:
        resolved = resolve_path(path_arg)
    except FileNotFoundError as e:
        sys.stderr.write(f"ERROR: {e}\n       Navigate into a repository before running git-graph, or use option --path\n")
        return 1

    found = find_git_dir(resolved)
    if not found:
        sys.stderr.write(f"ERROR: could not find repository at '{path_arg}'\n       Navigate into a repository before running git-graph, or use option --path\n")
        return 1
    _git_dir, workdir = found

    try:
        data = collect_commits(workdir, max_count=top_opts.get("max-count"), include_remotes=not top_opts.get("local"))
    except RuntimeError as e:
        sys.stderr.write(f"ERROR: {e}\n")
        return 1

    if top_opts.get("reverse"):
        data["commits"] = list(reversed(data["commits"]))

    fmt_name, custom = resolve_format(top_opts.get("format"))
    # The simple_render always uses oneline-equivalent.  This is a
    # best-effort fallback for more complex formats.
    out = simple_render(data, top_opts)
    sys.stdout.write(out)
    return 0


def main(argv=None):
    argv = list(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)

    try:
        parsed = parse_top_args(argv)
    except ParseError as e:
        sys.stderr.write(str(e))
        return 2

    opts = parsed["options"]

    if opts["help"]:
        sys.stdout.write(long_help())
        return 0
    if opts["version"]:
        sys.stdout.write(f"{PROG_NAME} {VERSION}\n")
        return 0

    if parsed["command"] == "model":
        return cmd_model(parsed["sub_args"], opts)
    if parsed["command"] == "help":
        sub = parsed["sub_args"]
        if not sub:
            sys.stdout.write(long_help())
            return 0
        if sub[0] == "model":
            sys.stdout.write(model_help())
            return 0
        if sub[0] == "help":
            sys.stdout.write(f"Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)\n\nUsage: {_exe_name()} help [COMMAND]...\n\nArguments:\n  [COMMAND]...  Print help for the subcommand(s)\n")
            return 0
        sys.stderr.write(f"error: unrecognized subcommand '{sub[0]}'\n\n" + usage_brief())
        return 2

    # Default: show graph.
    return do_graph(opts)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main() or 0)

def app_config_dir():
    # Linux: ~/.config/git-graph
    xdg = os.environ.get("XDG_CONFIG_HOME")
    if xdg:
        return Path(xdg) / "git-graph"
    return Path.home() / ".config" / "git-graph"


def models_dir():
    return app_config_dir() / "models"


def ensure_default_models():
    d = models_dir()
    if not d.exists():
        try:
            d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        except OSError:
            return
        (d / "git-flow.toml").write_text(_default_git_flow_toml(), encoding="utf-8")
        (d / "simple.toml").write_text(_default_simple_toml(), encoding="utf-8")
        (d / "none.toml").write_text(_default_none_toml(), encoding="utf-8")


def list_available_models():
    ensure_default_models()
    result = list(DEFAULT_MODELS)
    d = models_dir()
    try:
        entries = sorted(p.stem for p in d.iterdir() if p.suffix == ".toml")
    except OSError:
        entries = []
    for name in entries:
        if name not in result:
            result.append(name)
    return result

def resolve_path(p):
    """Mimic upstream's path handling for --path.

    Returns either an absolute Path, or raises FileNotFoundError if the path
    does not exist at all.
    """
    path = Path(p)
    try:
        resolved = path.resolve(strict=True)
    except FileNotFoundError as e:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"failed to resolve path '{p}': No such file or directory") from e
    return resolved


def find_git_dir(start):
    """Return (.git path, working dir) by walking up from start, or None."""
    cur = Path(start).resolve()
    while True:
        gd = cur / ".git"
        if gd.is_dir() or gd.is_file():
            return gd, cur
        if cur.parent == cur:
            return None
        cur = cur.parent


def read_repo_model(git_dir):
    """Read .git/git-graph.toml and return the model name or None."""
    f = Path(git_dir) / "git-graph.toml"
    if not f.is_file():
        return None
    try:
        text = f.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    except OSError:
        return None
    for line in text.splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#"):
            continue
        m = re.match(r'^model\s*=\s*["\'](.+)["\']\s*$', line)
        if m:
            return m.group(1)
    return None


def write_repo_model(git_dir, model):
    f = Path(git_dir) / "git-graph.toml"
    f.write_text(f'model = "{model}"\n', encoding="utf-8")

class ParseError(Exception):
    """Raised for user-facing CLI argument errors."""
    def __init__(self, message, usage=None):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.usage = usage if usage is not None else usage_brief()


TOP_OPTIONS_WITH_VALUE = {
    "-p": "path", "--path": "path",
    "-m": "model", "--model": "model",
    "-n": "max-count", "--max-count": "max-count",
    "--color": "color",
    "-f": "format", "--format": "format",
    "-s": "style", "--style": "style",
}

TOP_FLAGS = {
    "--skip-repo-owner-validation": "skip_owner",
    "--no-color": "no_color",
    "-r": "reverse", "--reverse": "reverse",
    "-l": "local", "--local": "local",
    "--svg": "svg",
    "-d": "debug", "--debug": "debug",
    "-S": "sparse", "--sparse": "sparse",
    "-h": "help", "--help": "help",
    "-V": "version", "--version": "version",
}


def parse_wrap(tokens):
    """Parse zero or more tokens for the -w/--wrap option."""
    # -w [<wrap>...] takes 0..N values until the next flag/subcommand.
    # An empty list means 'auto' (the default with no args is not documented,
    # but we treat it as 'auto').
    return list(tokens)


def _err_unexpected_arg(arg, usage=None):
    raise ParseError(f"error: unexpected argument '{arg}' found\n\n" + (usage or usage_brief()), usage=usage or usage_brief())


def _err_unrecognized_sub(name):
    raise ParseError(f"error: unrecognized subcommand '{name}'\n\n" + usage_brief())


def _err_missing_value(opt, usage=None):
    raise ParseError(f"error: a value is required for '{opt}' but none was supplied\n\n" + (usage or usage_brief()), usage=usage or usage_brief())


def parse_top_args(argv):
    """Parse top-level command line into an options dict.

    Returns: dict with keys:
      command: None | 'model' | 'help'
      sub_args: list of remaining args for the subcommand
      options: parsed top-level options
    """
    opts = {
        "path": None,
        "model": None,
        "max-count": None,
        "color": "auto",
        "format": None,
        "style": None,
        "wrap": None,
        "skip_owner": False,
        "no_color": False,
        "reverse": False,
        "local": False,
        "svg": False,
        "debug": False,
        "sparse": False,
        "help": False,
        "version": False,
    }

    i = 0
    command = None
    sub_args = []

    # A small helper: split '--foo=bar' into ('--foo', 'bar').
    def split_eq(tok):
        if tok.startswith("--") and "=" in tok:
            k, v = tok.split("=", 1)
            return k, v
        return tok, None

    while i < len(argv):
        tok = argv[i]

        # Subcommand detection – only the first non-option token matters.
        if tok == "model":
            sub_args = argv[i + 1 :]
            command = "model"
            return {"command": command, "sub_args": sub_args, "options": opts}
        if tok == "help":
            sub_args = argv[i + 1 :]
            command = "help"
            return {"command": command, "sub_args": sub_args, "options": opts}

        if tok.startswith("--"):
            key, val = split_eq(tok)
            if key in TOP_OPTIONS_WITH_VALUE:
                name = TOP_OPTIONS_WITH_VALUE[key]
                if val is not None:
                    opts[name] = val
                    i += 1
                    continue
                if i + 1 >= len(argv):
                    _err_missing_value(key)
                opts[name] = argv[i + 1]
                i += 2
                continue
            if key == "--wrap":
                # Consume 0..N non-option arguments.
                if val is not None:
                    wrap_tokens = [val]
                    i += 1
                else:
                    i += 1
                    wrap_tokens = []
                    while i < len(argv) and not argv[i].startswith("-") and argv[i] not in ("model", "help"):
                        wrap_tokens.append(argv[i])
                        i += 1
                opts["wrap"] = wrap_tokens
                continue
            if key in TOP_FLAGS:
                if val is not None:
                    if key in ("--help",):
                        raise ParseError(
                            f"error: unexpected value '{val}' for '--help' found; no more were expected\n\n"
                            f"Usage: {_exe_name()} --help\n\n"
                            "For more information, try '--help'.\n",
                        )
                    _err_unexpected_arg(tok)
                opts[TOP_FLAGS[key]] = True
                i += 1
                continue
            _err_unexpected_arg(tok)

        if tok.startswith("-") and tok != "-":
            # Short flag(s).  Support clustering of boolean flags, and a value
            # for the last option that requires one.
            j = 1
            while j < len(tok):
                c = "-" + tok[j]
                if c in TOP_OPTIONS_WITH_VALUE:
                    name = TOP_OPTIONS_WITH_VALUE[c]
                    rest = tok[j + 1 :]
                    if rest.startswith("="):
                        rest = rest[1:]
                    if rest:
                        opts[name] = rest
                        j = len(tok)
                        break
                    else:
                        if i + 1 >= len(argv):
                            _err_missing_value(c)
                        opts[name] = argv[i + 1]
                        i += 1
                        j = len(tok)
                        break
                elif c == "-w":
                    rest = tok[j + 1 :]
                    if rest.startswith("="):
                        rest = rest[1:]
                    if rest:
                        wrap_tokens = [rest]
                    else:
                        wrap_tokens = []
                    i += 1
                    while i < len(argv) and not argv[i].startswith("-") and argv[i] not in ("model", "help"):
                        wrap_tokens.append(argv[i])
                        i += 1
                    opts["wrap"] = wrap_tokens
                    j = None
                    break
                elif c in TOP_FLAGS:
                    opts[TOP_FLAGS[c]] = True
                    j += 1
                else:
                    _err_unexpected_arg(tok)
            if j is None:
                continue
            i += 1
            continue

        # A bare positional token – treat as unrecognised subcommand.
        _err_unrecognized_sub(tok)

    return {"command": command, "sub_args": sub_args, "options": opts}


def parse_model_args(argv):
    opts = {"list": False, "help": False, "model": None}
    i = 0
    while i < len(argv):
        tok = argv[i]
        if tok in ("-l", "--list"):
            opts["list"] = True
            i += 1
            continue
        if tok in ("-h", "--help"):
            opts["help"] = True
            i += 1
            continue
        if tok.startswith("-"):
            usage = usage_brief_model()
            tip = ""
            if tok.startswith("--"):
                tip = f"  tip: to pass '{tok}' as a value, use '-- {tok}'\n\n"
            raise ParseError(
                f"error: unexpected argument '{tok}' found\n\n{tip}{usage}",
                usage=usage,
            )
        if opts["model"] is None:
            opts["model"] = tok
            i += 1
            continue
        raise ParseError(
            f"error: unexpected argument '{tok}' found\n\n" + usage_brief_model(),
            usage=usage_brief_model(),
        )
    return opts

def cmd_model(args, top_opts):
    try:
        parsed = parse_model_args(args)
    except ParseError as e:
        sys.stderr.write(str(e))
        sys.exit(2)

    if parsed["help"]:
        sys.stdout.write(model_help())
        return 0

    if parsed["list"]:
        for name in list_available_models():
            print(name)
        return 0

    # Need a repository.
    path_arg = top_opts.get("path") or "."
    try:
        resolved = resolve_path(path_arg)
    except FileNotFoundError as e:
        sys.stderr.write(f"ERROR: {e}\n       Navigate into a repository before running git-graph, or use option --path\n")
        return 1

    found = find_git_dir(resolved)
    if not found:
        sys.stderr.write(f"ERROR: could not find repository at '{path_arg}'\n       Navigate into a repository before running git-graph, or use option --path\n")
        return 1
    git_dir, _workdir = found

    if parsed["model"] is None:
        current = read_repo_model(git_dir)
        if current is None:
            sys.stdout.write("No branching model set")
        else:
            sys.stdout.write(current)
        return 0

    # Set model.
    available = list_available_models()
    if parsed["model"] not in available:
        sys.stderr.write(
            f"ERROR: No branching model named '{parsed['model']}' found in {models_dir()}\n"
            f"       Available models are: {', '.join(available)}\n"
        )
        return 1

    write_repo_model(git_dir, parsed["model"])
    sys.stdout.write(f"Branching model set to '{parsed['model']}'")
    return 0

def resolve_style(name):
    if name is None:
        return STYLES["normal"]
    allowed = ["normal", "thin", "round", "bold", "double", "ascii"]
    # Prefix match including first-character abbreviation.
    if name in allowed:
        return STYLES[name]
    if len(name) >= 1:
        for a in allowed:
            if a.startswith(name):
                return STYLES[a]
    sys.stderr.write(
        f"Unknown characters/style '{name}'. Must be one of [normal|thin|round|bold|double|ascii]\n"
    )
    sys.exit(1)


def resolve_format(name):
    """Return canonical format name or a custom format string."""
    if name is None:
        return ("oneline", None)
    presets = ["oneline", "short", "medium", "full"]
    if name in presets:
        return (name, None)
    # First-character abbreviation
    if len(name) == 1:
        for p in presets:
            if p[0] == name[0]:
                return (p, None)
    return ("custom", name)

ANSI_RESET = "\x1b[0m"
COLOR_NAMES = {
    "black": 0, "red": 1, "green": 2, "yellow": 3,
    "blue": 4, "magenta": 5, "cyan": 6, "white": 7,
    "bright_black": 8, "bright_red": 9, "bright_green": 10, "bright_yellow": 11,
    "bright_blue": 12, "bright_magenta": 13, "bright_cyan": 14, "bright_white": 15,
}


def ansi_fg(color):
    if color is None:
        return ""
    if isinstance(color, int):
        return f"\x1b[38;5;{color}m"
    if color.isdigit():
        return f"\x1b[38;5;{int(color)}m"
    if color in COLOR_NAMES:
        return f"\x1b[38;5;{COLOR_NAMES[color]}m"
    return ""


class Colorizer:
    def __init__(self, enabled):
        self.enabled = enabled

    def wrap(self, text, color):
        if not self.enabled or not color:
            return text
        prefix = ansi_fg(color)
        if not prefix:
            return text
        return f"{prefix}{text}{ANSI_RESET}"


def decide_color(top_opts):
    if top_opts.get("no_color"):
        return False
    mode = top_opts.get("color") or "auto"
    if mode == "always":
        return True
    if mode == "never":
        return False
    if mode == "auto":
        return sys.stdout.isatty()
    sys.stderr.write(f"Unknown color mode '{mode}'. Supports [auto|always|never].\n")
    sys.exit(1)

def run_git(args, cwd):
    """Invoke `git` and return stdout as text."""
    env = os.environ.copy()
    env["GIT_PAGER"] = "cat"
    env["LC_ALL"] = "C"
    try:
        out = subprocess.run(
            ["git"] + args,
            cwd=str(cwd),
            env=env,
            check=True,
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
        )
    except FileNotFoundError:
        sys.stderr.write("ERROR: git not found on PATH\n")
        sys.exit(1)
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
        raise RuntimeError(e.stderr.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
    return out.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace")


def collect_commits(workdir, max_count=None, include_remotes=True):
    """Return list of commits and refs.

    Each commit is a dict with keys: id, short, parents (list of short),
    parents_full, subject, body, author, committer, author_date, commit_date,
    author_email, committer_email, author_short, commit_short.
    """
    # Gather refs first.
    refs_out = run_git(["for-each-ref", "--format=%(objectname) %(refname)"], workdir)
    refs = {}   # full_sha -> list of labels in display order
    for line in refs_out.strip().splitlines():
        if not line:
            continue
        sha, refname = line.split(" ", 1)
        if refname.startswith("refs/heads/"):
            label = refname[len("refs/heads/"):]
        elif refname.startswith("refs/remotes/"):
            if not include_remotes:
                continue
            label = refname[len("refs/remotes/"):]
        elif refname.startswith("refs/tags/"):
            label = "tag: " + refname[len("refs/tags/"):]
        else:
            label = refname
        refs.setdefault(sha, []).append(label)

    # HEAD
    try:
        head_ref = run_git(["symbolic-ref", "-q", "HEAD"], workdir).strip()
    except RuntimeError:
        head_ref = ""
    head_sha = run_git(["rev-parse", "HEAD"], workdir).strip()

    head_branch = None
    if head_ref.startswith("refs/heads/"):
        head_branch = head_ref[len("refs/heads/"):]

    # Build git log invocation.
    fmt = "%x1f".join(["%H", "%h", "%P", "%p", "%an", "%ae", "%ad", "%cn", "%ce", "%cd", "%s", "%b"])
    log_args = [
        "log",
        "--format=%x1e" + fmt + "%x1e",
        "--date=default",
        "--all",
    ]
    if not include_remotes:
        log_args = [x for x in log_args if x != "--all"]
        log_args.append("--branches")
        log_args.append("--tags")
    if max_count is not None:
        log_args.insert(1, f"-n{max_count}")

    raw = run_git(log_args, workdir)
    # Records are delimited by \x1e.
    records = [r for r in raw.split("\x1e") if r.strip()]
    commits = []
    for rec in records:
        rec = rec.rstrip("\n")
        fields = rec.split("\x1f")
        if len(fields) < 12:
            continue
        H, h, P, p, an, ae, ad, cn, ce, cd, s, b = fields[:12]
        commits.append({
            "id": H,
            "short": h,
            "parents_full": P.split() if P else [],
            "parents_short": p.split() if p else [],
            "author": an, "author_email": ae, "author_date": ad,
            "committer": cn, "committer_email": ce, "committer_date": cd,
            "subject": s,
            "body": b.strip("\n"),
        })

    return {
        "commits": commits,
        "refs": refs,
        "head_sha": head_sha,
        "head_branch": head_branch,
    }

def refs_label(commit, data):
    """Return decoration string like '(HEAD -> master, feature/foo)'."""
    labels = []
    sha = commit["id"]
    entries = list(data["refs"].get(sha, []))
    head_branch = data["head_branch"]

    # Separate tags from branches to emit tags in brackets.
    tag_labels = []
    branch_labels = []
    for e in entries:
        if e.startswith("tag: "):
            tag_labels.append(e[len("tag: "):])
        else:
            branch_labels.append(e)

    if head_branch and head_branch in branch_labels:
        idx = branch_labels.index(head_branch)
        branch_labels.pop(idx)
        first = f"HEAD -> {head_branch}"
        branch_labels.insert(0, first)
    elif sha == data["head_sha"] and head_branch is None:
        branch_labels.insert(0, "HEAD")

    return branch_labels, tag_labels


def format_oneline(commit, data, colorizer, branch_colors_for_commit, tag_color):
    branch_labels, tag_labels = refs_label(commit, data)
    parts = [colorizer.wrap(commit["short"], "bright_yellow")]
    if branch_labels:
        inner = []
        for lbl in branch_labels:
            if lbl.startswith("HEAD"):
                # Color the 'HEAD ->' in cyan, branch in its colour.
                if " -> " in lbl:
                    head, branch = lbl.split(" -> ", 1)
                    inner.append(
                        colorizer.wrap(f"{head} ->", "bright_cyan") + " "
                        + colorizer.wrap(branch, branch_colors_for_commit or "white")
                    )
                else:
                    inner.append(colorizer.wrap(lbl, "bright_cyan"))
            else:
                inner.append(colorizer.wrap(lbl, branch_colors_for_commit or "white"))
        parts.append("(" + ", ".join(inner) + ")")
    if tag_labels:
        parts.append("[" + ", ".join(colorizer.wrap(t, tag_color) for t in tag_labels) + "]")
    parts.append(commit["subject"])
    return " ".join(parts)


def simple_render(data, top_opts):
    style = resolve_style(top_opts.get("style"))
    colorizer = Colorizer(decide_color(top_opts))

    # Trivial renderer: every commit on column 0 with bullet glyph, no branching shown.
    lines = []
    for c in data["commits"]:
        is_merge = len(c["parents_full"]) > 1
        dot = style["merge_dot"] if is_merge else style["commit_dot"]
        dot = colorizer.wrap(dot, "white")
        text = format_oneline(c, data, colorizer, "white", "bright_green")
        lines.append(f" {dot}  {text}")
    return "\n".join(lines) + ("\n" if lines else "")

# Top-level dispatch                                                          #
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

def do_graph(top_opts):
    """Handle the default (no-subcommand) behaviour."""
    # Early validation that can occur before any path work.
    color_mode = top_opts.get("color") or "auto"
    if not top_opts.get("no_color") and color_mode not in ("auto", "always", "never"):
        sys.stderr.write(f"Unknown color mode '{color_mode}'. Supports [auto|always|never].\n")
        return 1

    # Max-count validation.
    mc = top_opts.get("max-count")
    if mc is not None:
        try:
            mc_i = int(mc)
            if mc_i <= 0:
                raise ValueError
            top_opts["max-count"] = mc_i
        except ValueError:
            sys.stderr.write(f"Option max-count must be a positive number, but got '{mc}'\n")
            return 1

    # Wrap validation.
    wrap = top_opts.get("wrap")
    if wrap is not None:
        for w in wrap:
            if w in ("auto", "none"):
                continue
            try:
                int(w)
            except ValueError:
                sys.stderr.write(f"ERROR: Can't parse option --wrap '{w}' to integers.\n")
                return 1

    # Style validation (resolve_style may exit).
    if top_opts.get("style") is not None:
        resolve_style(top_opts["style"])

    # Path handling.
    path_arg = top_opts.get("path") or "."
    try:
        resolved = resolve_path(path_arg)
    except FileNotFoundError as e:
        sys.stderr.write(f"ERROR: {e}\n       Navigate into a repository before running git-graph, or use option --path\n")
        return 1

    found = find_git_dir(resolved)
    if not found:
        sys.stderr.write(f"ERROR: could not find repository at '{path_arg}'\n       Navigate into a repository before running git-graph, or use option --path\n")
        return 1
    _git_dir, workdir = found

    try:
        data = collect_commits(workdir, max_count=top_opts.get("max-count"), include_remotes=not top_opts.get("local"))
    except RuntimeError as e:
        sys.stderr.write(f"ERROR: {e}\n")
        return 1

    if top_opts.get("reverse"):
        data["commits"] = list(reversed(data["commits"]))

    fmt_name, custom = resolve_format(top_opts.get("format"))
    # The simple_render always uses oneline-equivalent.  This is a
    # best-effort fallback for more complex formats.
    out = simple_render(data, top_opts)
    sys.stdout.write(out)
    return 0


def main(argv=None):
    argv = list(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)

    try:
        parsed = parse_top_args(argv)
    except ParseError as e:
        sys.stderr.write(str(e))
        return 2

    opts = parsed["options"]

    if opts["help"]:
        sys.stdout.write(long_help())
        return 0
    if opts["version"]:
        sys.stdout.write(f"{PROG_NAME} {VERSION}\n")
        return 0

    if parsed["command"] == "model":
        return cmd_model(parsed["sub_args"], opts)
    if parsed["command"] == "help":
        sub = parsed["sub_args"]
        if not sub:
            sys.stdout.write(long_help())
            return 0
        if sub[0] == "model":
            sys.stdout.write(model_help())
            return 0
        if sub[0] == "help":
            sys.stdout.write(f"Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)\n\nUsage: {_exe_name()} help [COMMAND]...\n\nArguments:\n  [COMMAND]...  Print help for the subcommand(s)\n")
            return 0
        sys.stderr.write(f"error: unrecognized subcommand '{sub[0]}'\n\n" + usage_brief())
        return 2

    # Default: show graph.
    return do_graph(opts)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main() or 0)

def resolve_path(p):

    path = Path(p)

    return resolved

    """Return (.git path, working dir) by walking up from start, or None."""
    cur = Path(start).resolve()
    while True:
        gd = cur / ".git"
        if gd.is_dir() or gd.is_file():
            return gd, cur
        if cur.parent == cur:
            return None
        cur = cur.parent

    """Read .git/git-graph.toml and return the model name or None."""
    f = Path(git_dir) / "git-graph.toml"
    if not f.is_file():
        return None
    try:
        text = f.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    except OSError:
        return None
    for line in text.splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#"):
            continue
        m = re.match(r'^model\s*=\s*["\'](.+)["\']\s*$', line)
        if m:
            return m.group(1)
    return None

    raise ParseError(f"error: unrecognized subcommand '{name}'\n\n" + usage_brief())


def _err_missing_value(opt, usage=None):
    raise ParseError(f"error: a value is required for '{opt}' but none was supplied\n\n" + (usage or usage_brief()), usage=usage or usage_brief())


def parse_top_args(argv):
    """Parse top-level command line into an options dict.

    Returns: dict with keys:
      command: None | 'model' | 'help'
      sub_args: list of remaining args for the subcommand
      options: parsed top-level options
    """
    opts = {
        "path": None,
        "model": None,
        "max-count": None,
        "color": "auto",
        "format": None,
        "style": None,
        "wrap": None,
        "skip_owner": False,
        "no_color": False,
        "reverse": False,
        "local": False,
        "svg": False,
        "debug": False,
        "sparse": False,
        "help": False,
        "version": False,
    }

    i = 0
    command = None
    sub_args = []

    # A small helper: split '--foo=bar' into ('--foo', 'bar').
    def split_eq(tok):
        if tok.startswith("--") and "=" in tok:
            k, v = tok.split("=", 1)
            return k, v
        return tok, None

    while i < len(argv):
        tok = argv[i]

        # Subcommand detection – only the first non-option token matters.
        if tok == "model":
            sub_args = argv[i + 1 :]
            command = "model"
            return {"command": command, "sub_args": sub_args, "options": opts}
        if tok == "help":
            sub_args = argv[i + 1 :]
            command = "help"
            return {"command": command, "sub_args": sub_args, "options": opts}

        if tok.startswith("--"):
            key, val = split_eq(tok)
            if key in TOP_OPTIONS_WITH_VALUE:
                name = TOP_OPTIONS_WITH_VALUE[key]
                if val is not None:
                    opts[name] = val
                    i += 1
                    continue
                if i + 1 >= len(argv):
                    _err_missing_value(key)
                opts[name] = argv[i + 1]
                i += 2
                continue
            if key == "--wrap":
                # Consume 0..N non-option arguments.
                if val is not None:
                    wrap_tokens = [val]
                    i += 1
                else:
                    i += 1
                    wrap_tokens = []
                    while i < len(argv) and not argv[i].startswith("-") and argv[i] not in ("model", "help"):
                        wrap_tokens.append(argv[i])
                        i += 1
                opts["wrap"] = wrap_tokens
                continue
            if key in TOP_FLAGS:
                if val is not None:
                    if key in ("--help",):
                        raise ParseError(
                            f"error: unexpected value '{val}' for '--help' found; no more were expected\n\n"
                            f"Usage: {_exe_name()} --help\n\n"
                            "For more information, try '--help'.\n",
                        )
                    _err_unexpected_arg(tok)
                opts[TOP_FLAGS[key]] = True
                i += 1
                continue
            _err_unexpected_arg(tok)

        if tok.startswith("-") and tok != "-":
            # Short flag(s).  Support clustering of boolean flags, and a value
            # for the last option that requires one.
            j = 1
            while j < len(tok):
                c = "-" + tok[j]
                if c in TOP_OPTIONS_WITH_VALUE:
                    name = TOP_OPTIONS_WITH_VALUE[c]
                    rest = tok[j + 1 :]
                    if rest.startswith("="):
                        rest = rest[1:]
                    if rest:
                        opts[name] = rest
                        j = len(tok)
                        break
                    else:
                        if i + 1 >= len(argv):
                            _err_missing_value(c)
                        opts[name] = argv[i + 1]
                        i += 1
                        j = len(tok)
                        break
                elif c == "-w":
                    rest = tok[j + 1 :]
                    if rest.startswith("="):
                        rest = rest[1:]
                    if rest:
                        wrap_tokens = [rest]
                    else:
                        wrap_tokens = []
                    i += 1
                    while i < len(argv) and not argv[i].startswith("-") and argv[i] not in ("model", "help"):
                        wrap_tokens.append(argv[i])
                        i += 1
                    opts["wrap"] = wrap_tokens
                    j = None
                    break
                elif c in TOP_FLAGS:
                    opts[TOP_FLAGS[c]] = True
                    j += 1
                else:
                    _err_unexpected_arg(tok)
            if j is None:
                continue
            i += 1
            continue

        # A bare positional token – treat as unrecognised subcommand.
        _err_unrecognized_sub(tok)

    return {"command": command, "sub_args": sub_args, "options": opts}


def parse_model_args(argv):
    opts = {"list": False, "help": False, "model": None}
    i = 0
    while i < len(argv):
        tok = argv[i]
        if tok in ("-l", "--list"):
            opts["list"] = True
            i += 1
            continue
        if tok in ("-h", "--help"):
            opts["help"] = True
            i += 1
            continue
        if tok.startswith("-"):
            usage = usage_brief_model()
            tip = ""
            if tok.startswith("--"):
                tip = f"  tip: to pass '{tok}' as a value, use '-- {tok}'\n\n"
            raise ParseError(
                f"error: unexpected argument '{tok}' found\n\n{tip}{usage}",
                usage=usage,
            )
        if opts["model"] is None:
            opts["model"] = tok
            i += 1
            continue
        raise ParseError(
            f"error: unexpected argument '{tok}' found\n\n" + usage_brief_model(),
            usage=usage_brief_model(),
        )
    return opts

        "cross": "+",

    },
}
STYLES["thin"] = STYLES["normal"]


def resolve_style(name):
    if name is None:
        return STYLES["normal"]
    allowed = ["normal", "thin", "round", "bold", "double", "ascii"]
    # Prefix match including first-character abbreviation.
    if name in allowed:
        return STYLES[name]
    if len(name) >= 1:
        for a in allowed:
            if a.startswith(name):
                return STYLES[a]
    sys.stderr.write(
        f"Unknown characters/style '{name}'. Must be one of [normal|thin|round|bold|double|ascii]\n"
    )
    sys.exit(1)


def resolve_format(name):
    """Return canonical format name or a custom format string."""
    if name is None:
        return ("oneline", None)
    presets = ["oneline", "short", "medium", "full"]
    if name in presets:
        return (name, None)
    # First-character abbreviation
    if len(name) == 1:
        for p in presets:
            if p[0] == name[0]:
                return (p, None)
    return ("custom", name)

# Colour support                                                              #

ANSI_RESET = "\x1b[0m"
COLOR_NAMES = {
    "black": 0, "red": 1, "green": 2, "yellow": 3,
    "blue": 4, "magenta": 5, "cyan": 6, "white": 7,
    "bright_black": 8, "bright_red": 9, "bright_green": 10, "bright_yellow": 11,
    "bright_blue": 12, "bright_magenta": 13, "bright_cyan": 14, "bright_white": 15,
}


def ansi_fg(color):
    if color is None:
        return ""
    if isinstance(color, int):
        return f"\x1b[38;5;{color}m"
    if color.isdigit():
        return f"\x1b[38;5;{int(color)}m"
    if color in COLOR_NAMES:
        return f"\x1b[38;5;{COLOR_NAMES[color]}m"
    return ""


class Colorizer:
    def __init__(self, enabled):
        self.enabled = enabled

    def wrap(self, text, color):
        if not self.enabled or not color:
            return text
        prefix = ansi_fg(color)
        if not prefix:
            return text
        return f"{prefix}{text}{ANSI_RESET}"


def decide_color(top_opts):
    if top_opts.get("no_color"):
        return False
    mode = top_opts.get("color") or "auto"
    if mode == "always":
        return True
    if mode == "never":
        return False
    if mode == "auto":
        return sys.stdout.isatty()
    sys.stderr.write(f"Unknown color mode '{mode}'. Supports [auto|always|never].\n")
    sys.exit(1)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Git log data collection                                                     #
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

def run_git(args, cwd):
    """Invoke `git` and return stdout as text."""
    env = os.environ.copy()
    env["GIT_PAGER"] = "cat"
    env["LC_ALL"] = "C"
    try:
        out = subprocess.run(
            ["git"] + args,
            cwd=str(cwd),
            env=env,
            check=True,
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
        )
    except FileNotFoundError:
        sys.stderr.write("ERROR: git not found on PATH\n")
        sys.exit(1)
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
        raise RuntimeError(e.stderr.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
    return out.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace")


def collect_commits(workdir, max_count=None, include_remotes=True):
    """Return list of commits and refs.

    Each commit is a dict with keys: id, short, parents (list of short),
    parents_full, subject, body, author, committer, author_date, commit_date,
    author_email, committer_email, author_short, commit_short.
    """
    # Gather refs first.
    refs_out = run_git(["for-each-ref", "--format=%(objectname) %(refname)"], workdir)
    refs = {}   # full_sha -> list of labels in display order
    for line in refs_out.strip().splitlines():
        if not line:
            continue
        sha, refname = line.split(" ", 1)
        if refname.startswith("refs/heads/"):
            label = refname[len("refs/heads/"):]
        elif refname.startswith("refs/remotes/"):
            if not include_remotes:
                continue
            label = refname[len("refs/remotes/"):]
        elif refname.startswith("refs/tags/"):
            label = "tag: " + refname[len("refs/tags/"):]
        else:
            label = refname
        refs.setdefault(sha, []).append(label)

    # HEAD
    try:
        head_ref = run_git(["symbolic-ref", "-q", "HEAD"], workdir).strip()
    except RuntimeError:
        head_ref = ""
    head_sha = run_git(["rev-parse", "HEAD"], workdir).strip()

    head_branch = None
    if head_ref.startswith("refs/heads/"):
        head_branch = head_ref[len("refs/heads/"):]

    # Build git log invocation.
    fmt = "%x1f".join(["%H", "%h", "%P", "%p", "%an", "%ae", "%ad", "%cn", "%ce", "%cd", "%s", "%b"])
    log_args = [
        "log",
        "--format=%x1e" + fmt + "%x1e",
        "--date=default",
        "--all",
    ]
    if not include_remotes:
        log_args = [x for x in log_args if x != "--all"]
        log_args.append("--branches")
        log_args.append("--tags")
    if max_count is not None:
        log_args.insert(1, f"-n{max_count}")

    raw = run_git(log_args, workdir)
    # Records are delimited by \x1e.
    records = [r for r in raw.split("\x1e") if r.strip()]
    commits = []
    for rec in records:
        rec = rec.rstrip("\n")
        fields = rec.split("\x1f")
        if len(fields) < 12:
            continue
        H, h, P, p, an, ae, ad, cn, ce, cd, s, b = fields[:12]
        commits.append({
            "id": H,
            "short": h,
            "parents_full": P.split() if P else [],
            "parents_short": p.split() if p else [],
            "author": an, "author_email": ae, "author_date": ad,
            "committer": cn, "committer_email": ce, "committer_date": cd,
            "subject": s,
            "body": b.strip("\n"),
        })

    return {
        "commits": commits,
        "refs": refs,
        "head_sha": head_sha,
        "head_branch": head_branch,
    }


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Graph rendering                                                             #
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

def refs_label(commit, data):
    """Return decoration string like '(HEAD -> master, feature/foo)'."""
    labels = []
    sha = commit["id"]
    entries = list(data["refs"].get(sha, []))
    head_branch = data["head_branch"]

    # Separate tags from branches to emit tags in brackets.
    tag_labels = []
    branch_labels = []
    for e in entries:
        if e.startswith("tag: "):
            tag_labels.append(e[len("tag: "):])
        else:
            branch_labels.append(e)

    if head_branch and head_branch in branch_labels:
        idx = branch_labels.index(head_branch)
        branch_labels.pop(idx)
        first = f"HEAD -> {head_branch}"
        branch_labels.insert(0, first)
    elif sha == data["head_sha"] and head_branch is None:
        branch_labels.insert(0, "HEAD")

    return branch_labels, tag_labels


def format_oneline(commit, data, colorizer, branch_colors_for_commit, tag_color):
    branch_labels, tag_labels = refs_label(commit, data)
    parts = [colorizer.wrap(commit["short"], "bright_yellow")]
    if branch_labels:
        inner = []
        for lbl in branch_labels:
            if lbl.startswith("HEAD"):
                # Color the 'HEAD ->' in cyan, branch in its colour.
                if " -> " in lbl:
                    head, branch = lbl.split(" -> ", 1)
                    inner.append(
                        colorizer.wrap(f"{head} ->", "bright_cyan") + " "
                        + colorizer.wrap(branch, branch_colors_for_commit or "white")
                    )
                else:
                    inner.append(colorizer.wrap(lbl, "bright_cyan"))
            else:
                inner.append(colorizer.wrap(lbl, branch_colors_for_commit or "white"))
        parts.append("(" + ", ".join(inner) + ")")
    if tag_labels:
        parts.append("[" + ", ".join(colorizer.wrap(t, tag_color) for t in tag_labels) + "]")
    parts.append(commit["subject"])
    return " ".join(parts)


def simple_render(data, top_opts):
    style = resolve_style(top_opts.get("style"))
    colorizer = Colorizer(decide_color(top_opts))

    # Trivial renderer: every commit on column 0 with bullet glyph, no branching shown.
    lines = []
    for c in data["commits"]:
        is_merge = len(c["parents_full"]) > 1
        dot = style["merge_dot"] if is_merge else style["commit_dot"]
        dot = colorizer.wrap(dot, "white")
        text = format_oneline(c, data, colorizer, "white", "bright_green")
        lines.append(f" {dot}  {text}")
    return "\n".join(lines) + ("\n" if lines else "")
